# secobserve_license_group_authorization_group_member (Resource)

Grants every member of an authorization group manage rights on a license group, instead of one membership per user.

Not copied by `secobserve_license_group`'s upstream copy action -- irrelevant here since this provider does not expose that action, but worth knowing if a group was seeded that way outside Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "secobserve_authorization_group" "legal" {
  name = "Legal"
}

resource "secobserve_license_group_authorization_group_member" "legal_team" {
  license_group       = secobserve_license_group.permissive.id
  authorization_group = secobserve_authorization_group.legal.id
  is_manager          = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `authorization_group` (Number) Id of the authorization group. Immutable: a change replaces the membership.
- `license_group` (Number) Id of the license group. Immutable: SecObserve rejects moving a membership, so a change replaces it.

### Optional

- `is_manager` (Boolean) Whether members of this authorization group can manage the license group itself: edit it, and add or remove other members and licenses.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric id of the membership.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = secobserve_license_group_authorization_group_member.legal_team
  id = "4/3"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <license group id>/<authorization group id>.
terraform import secobserve_license_group_authorization_group_member.legal_team "4/3"
```
